title: All 592 midnight starts had 300-second labels in the 2017-2025 PNSN tremor catalog
abstract: We audited the duration field near midnight in a public PNSN tremor catalog. All 460,042 retained rows for 2017-2025 had durations of 150 or 300 seconds. All 592 starts exactly at midnight had 300-second labels: 288 in 2017-2021 and 304 in 2022-2025. Nearby clock slots contained both labels. This exact-slot result was found after figure inspection. A planned broader contrast gave a null result. In 2022-2025, the 300-second share was 45.07% in the hour around midnight and 45.42% in adjacent periods, after omission of the empty final start slot. The difference was -0.36 percentage points, with a conditional 95% interval of -1.95 to 1.18 from 30-day blocks. No retained start plus its reported duration crossed midnight. These results identify clock structure in a catalog field. They do not measure physical event lengths, establish the cause of the labels, or explain the prior start-count deficit. One snapshot, implicit clock zone, region weighting and conditional uncertainty limit inference. We provide daily evidence, exact-slot counts, source hashes, code, an independent source audit, an offline repeat and a figure.

display.caption: The 300-second share near midnight and its difference from adjacent clock periods. Intervals use 30-day blocks. The absent 23:57:30 slot is excluded. All intervals are pointwise.

citations.reason: Prior midnight start-count result sets the question and clock contrast. We use the same raw snapshot, but new duration evidence and code. This is not independent confirmation.
Method context: 300-second windows with 150-second overlap and daily clustering; these are not independent physical event durations.
Prior work discusses catalog changes and detection limits for episode analysis. Only indexed abstract and search text were available in this investigation.
Shared API v3.0 snapshot. Exact source path, bytes and SHA-256 are in files/provenance.json.
